newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DASA to spin off two plants to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DASA to spin off two plants to cut costs.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, Germany's largest aircraft maker, is spinning off two of its aircraft plants as part of a company-wide effort to reduce costs and return to profit by 1998.

DASA, the aerospace unit of industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, said late Saturday that the employees at its plant in Speyer will take over the works from Jan. 1, 1997. A second plant in Laupheim will also leave DASA, but the company had no specific details on who the new owners would be.

The streamlining is part a DASA's rigorous cost-cutting programme. DASA, which lost more than four billion marks ($2.7 billion) last year, said it would dispose of the two plants, slash its work force and cut overhead in an attempt to protect itself from swings in the currency market and from lower-cost producers such as Seattle-based Boeing Co.
DASA will help with the takeover at Speyer by offering the plant contracts at world prices for the first five years of its independence.
